data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Statistical independence between random variables is mathematically precise; engine separation is an architectural binary.","Decorrelation in the limit of infinite samples does not guarantee decorrelation on a single specific claim."],"overturn_conditions":["If decorrelation is demonstrably achievable only through engine separation, the mechanist position is restored as necessary.","If the perturbation test is shown to be gameable by a restater (verdict flips for irrelevant reasons), the operationalization is incomplete."],"shared_structure":["Independence is operationalized as error decorrelation between producer and verifier.","Multiple routes (separate training, deterministic oracle, frozen module) can in principle achieve decorrelation.","No single route is necessary if the property is secured."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001","SRC_002","SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["The perturbation-sensitivity test from single-run diagnostics operationalizes decorrelation at the run level: the verdict must respond to a decorrelated signal.","The covering principle unifies the mechanist (engine separation) and empiric (oracle execution) positions under one criterion."]},"claim":"The necessity question is a category error: independence is a property of the evidential channel, not of the engine boundary. Two engines with correlated training data fail to independently verify, while a single engine consulting a deterministic oracle independently verifies. The covering principle is causal decorrelation of the verifier's verdict from the author's prior.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If decorrelation is shown to be insufficient (e.g., a decorrelated oracle that is nonetheless irrelevant to the claim), an additional relevance condition is required.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a single-engine frozen-module architecture cannot achieve decorrelation in practice, engine separation becomes necessary de facto even if not de jure.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Verification is genuine iff the checker's verdict is causally sensitive to an information source whose error distribution is decorrelated from the author's. Engine separation is one proxy for achieving decorrelation; deterministic oracles are another.
